stories.notes: Empty acceptance criteria and null spec on a complex cross-platform (GO, UP, MX) live preview feature. Openspec must first elaborate requirements and define technical scope for real-time rendering and state synchronization across platforms. Speckit then hardens with testability criteria, security checks (preview URL auth, sandbox isolation), and edge-case coverage. Both agents warranted due to complexity and zero existing specification.

agentContributions.notes: Story requests a new Live Preview capability for Contentstack CMS content. No acceptance criteria provided; VCs derived from the title/description intent. The central attachment point is useContent (236 callers) — all Contentstack components inherit content through it. Contentstack hosts are unreachable at test time, so VCs are written to our side of the boundary (what requests we make, how we handle responses, what we render given known data).

Openspec provided an empty acceptanceCriteria array with a note about the boundary-testing approach. I derived all 13 ACs from the story title/description and the four key files listed. CRITICAL CAVEAT: I could not read the actual file contents (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx), so my ACs are based on standard Contentstack live-preview patterns and the file names/roles described in the openspec note. The real implementation may use a specific SDK (e.g., @contentstack/live-preview-utils) or websocket mechanism that would make some ACs more specific or redundant. I strongly recommend a human review these ACs against the actual file contents. I structured ACs around: (1) preview request construction, (2) draft rendering, (3) real-time updates, (4) error/timeout fallback, (5) malformed data resilience, (6) preview teardown, (7) security/isolation from production, (8) cross-site parity, (9) useContent propagation, (10) ContentstackLink specifics, (11) update isolation, (12) new-draft entries, (13) interface conformance.

coordinatorReview.reviewNotes: Manifest paths all verified present (useContent.ts, contentstack.ts, contentCard.ts, ContentstackLink.tsx) — no missing files. Both agents contributed non-overlapping value: openspec scoped the technical boundary (identifying useContent as the 236-caller attachment point and the unreachable-Contentstack-host constraint), while speckit structured 13 verification criteria across security, edge cases, teardown, and isolation. However, speckit explicitly states it could not read the actual file contents and derived all VCs from standard Contentstack live-preview patterns and file-name inference rather than real code. The agent itself strongly recommends human review against actual file contents. This means VCs may not reflect the real SDK mechanism (e.g., @contentstack/live-preview-utils vs websocket), actual data flow through useContent, or existing patterns in contentstack.ts. Empty acceptanceCriteria on this brownfield ticket is expected by policy and not penalized. Human review needed to validate VCs against actual codebase before implementation.
